summary: Figure 3 shows Phantora's architecture for simulating distributed ML training performance while reusing real framework code. On the left, each Container runs an unmodified Training Script and Framework plus a minimally-modified PyTorch instrumented with a Phantora Tracer, alongside constructed Phantora NCCL and Phantora CUDA Runtime replacements. These emit computation and communication events (blue/green arrows) plus timestamp-synchronization signals (orange arrows) to a central Event Queue in the Phantora Simulator. The Event Queue dispatches computation events to a Computation Simulator, which profiles new (kernel, tensor-shape) combinations on a single real GPU via a Performance Estimation Cache, and communication events to an event-driven Network Simulator. Because only PyTorch's internals are patched at the Python runtime-patching level, applications cannot tell they are running on Phantora rather than a physical GPU cluster, letting Phantora reuse most of the existing ML software stack unmodified.
summary_zh: 图3展示Phantora架构：容器内未修改的训练脚本、框架与轻度修改的PyTorch通过Tracer把计算和通信事件送入模拟器的事件队列，分别交给计算模拟器（用单GPU分析核函数并缓存结果）和网络模拟器处理。
